messages.subject: Error with advanced sleeplog part4
parts:
Hi all,

I'm a PhD candidate currently using GGIR to analyse children's sleep actigraphy data along with sleep diary (advanced sleep log, formatted according to the guide), and I'm quite stuck with an error.

Below is the code I used:
             ## PART 4: Detection of Sleep vs SIB
             #-----------------------------------
             includenightcrit=6,
             sleeplogsep = ",",
             sleepwindowType = "TimeInBed",
             loglocation = loglocation,
             coln1 = 3,
             colid = 2,
             nnights = 7,
             sleeplogidnum = FALSE,
             #def.noc.sleep=c(1),
             nap_model = "hip3yr",
             # OUTPUT PARAMETERS
             do.visual = TRUE,
             outliers.only = FALSE,
             do.sibreport = TRUE,

And this is the error message I'm receiving: 
Part 4 Erreur dans nonwearlog[nwcnt, 2] <- S[i, curdatecol] : le nombre d'objets à remplacer n'est pas multiple de la taille du remplacement De plus : Messages d'avis : 1: Dans datecols > curdatecol : la taille d'un objet plus long n'est pas multiple de la taille d'un objet plus court 2: Dans onsetcols > curdatecol : la taille d'un objet plus long n'est pas multiple de la taille d'un objet plus court

Sorry I'm using French version! This indicates the message below, but it might be different than real Enlish version:

Part 4
Error in nonwearlog[nwcnt, 2] <- S[i, curdatecol]:
  the number of objects to replace is not multiple of the replacement size
In addition: Notification messages :
1: In datecols > curdatecol :
  the size of a longer object is not a multiple of the size of a shorter object
2: In onsetcols > curdatecol :
  the size of a longer object is not a multiple of the size of a shorter object
In English (using translator)

I assigned the ID and separators correctly. It seems the nonwearlog and other elements are generated within g.shell function, so I'm not assigning any elements by myself. And it makes me more confused :(

Thank you for this group and thank you in advance for your help.

Best,
Mihyeon

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error with advanced sleeplog part4
parts:
Dear Mihyeon,

Which version of GGIR are you using? Did you try the last version on GitHub?

Did you try isolating the source of the issue by narrowing the problem down to a single accelerometer file and a single sleep log entry? This would help to identify the source of the problem and makes it easier for me/others to help you. 

The error may indicate that there is a double date in the sleeplog. In the next GGIR release we will provide a more meaningful error about that. If not, then check carefully whether something else is incorrect in the sleeplog.

Note that g.shell.GGIR() is not needed, you can just use GGIR().

Vincent
